record.paper_title: On the Number and the Geometry of Hyperbolic Knots and Links with a Common Cyclic Branched Covering: Known Results and Open Problems
record.original_question: Let M be a closed orientable hyperbolic 3-manifold and let p be a fixed prime. Determine how many pairwise different knots and links in S^3 can have M as their p-fold cyclic branched covering, and describe how any such knots or links are related to one another.

evidence.quote: Problem 1.1: Given a closed orientable hyperbolic 3-manifold M and fixing a prime p, of how many different knots and links in the 3-sphere can M be a p-fold cyclic branched covering, and how are such knots or links related?

artifact.self_contained_problem: Let $M$ be a closed orientable hyperbolic 3-manifold and let $p$ be a fixed prime. Determine the maximum number of pairwise inequivalent knots and links in the 3-sphere $S^3$ that can have $M$ as their $p$-fold cyclic branched covering, and describe the relationship between any two such knots or links (for instance, via symmetries of $M$ or commensurability of their complements).
artifact.category_tag: Cyclic branched coverings of knots and links
artifact.status_search_result: Partial bounds are known: Mecchia–Zimmermann and related works show a hyperbolic 3-manifold can be a cyclic branched cover of at most finitely many knots in $S^3$ (e.g. at most fifteen in general, and at most six for odd prime order in the irreducible case). The general problem of an exact count and a complete description for all primes $p$ and for links remains open.

status_evidence.title: Hyperbolic 3-manifolds as cyclic branched coverings
status_evidence.snippet: A hyperbolic 3-manifold can be the cyclic branched cover of at most fifteen knots in S^3.
status_evidence.claim: Finite upper bounds are established, providing partial answers.

status_evidence.title: Finite group actions and cyclic branched covers of knots in S^3
status_evidence.snippet: Studies how knots K1 and K2 are related when their cyclic branched covers coincide.
status_evidence.claim: Relationship between such knots is partially understood via finite group actions.

status_evidence.title: Hyperbolic Knots and Cyclic Branched Covers (Publ. Mat.)
status_evidence.snippet: Bounds on the number of hyperbolic knots sharing a common cyclic branched cover.
status_evidence.claim: Partial results for hyperbolic knots; general problem remains open.
